questions.question: Does passing one gradient check prove a loss implementation is correct for all inputs?
options: No; it is evidence at tested inputs and must be combined with shape and objective checks
questions.explanation: Independent gradient calculations help expose errors, but finite test cases do not prove all behavior.
optionFeedback: An independent derivative or finite difference helps test AD. Reusing AD as its own expected answer cannot detect a shared objective error.
Independent gradient calculations help expose errors, but finite test cases do not prove all behavior.
Gradient checks are useful on CPU too. Their limits concern tested inputs, tolerances and objective correctness, not a requirement for TPUs.
